title: Why you replay conversations at night

scenes.say: They liked you more than you think.
After meeting someone new, many of us replay the awkward bits at night. Did I talk too much? Was that joke weird?
Researchers call this the liking gap. One explanation: you are busy judging your own performance, so you miss the signs they liked you.
In one Yale study, strangers chatted for about five minutes. Afterward, people underestimated how much their partner liked them.

data.title: How much did they like you?

scenes.say: Say you have lunch with a new colleague. All night you replay every pause. Next morning, they message first.

messages.text: Sorry, I went on about my old job yesterday
What? Best lunch all week. Same time Friday?

scenes.say: Across five studies, the gap showed up with lab strangers, workshop groups, and new college suitemates, where it lasted for months.
Next time, assume it went a little better than it felt. Send this to the friend who replays every chat.
